messages.subject: Proposal evaluation
messages.body_plain:
Mentors: I've had a quick look at each proposal and submitted a very short comment on each to
provide a preliminary categorization of them. From my time as org-admin with Claudia Beleites,
I know how difficult it can be to get a fair overview of the projects, since none of us have
sufficient breadth of expertise to be able to fully appreciate all of them. In some cases
I've asked the mentors to give some guidance to the rest of us, but we can all benefit from
well-considered input so we recommend a set of projects that will proceed to useful and
successful completion.

I urge you all to take a look at the proposals as soon as possible.

Best, John Nash

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

It's my first time as a mentor of GSoC and I don't know the customs to select the students.
I provided some comments on the proposal for my project.
I checked almost all proposals of the other students, what kind of feedback will be more useful?

There are two projects using rtweet: R Conference Events Explorer <https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/R-Conference-Events-Explorer> and R Community Explorer: Twitter <https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/R-Community-Explorer%3A-Twitter>.
I have become the maintainer of rtweet and I'm planning a major breaking release by the end of this year.
You might want to plan accordingly or use the unstable development version on github for the project.

Cheers,

Lluís

messages.subject: Re: Proposal evaluation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lluís, given how early we are in the process and the number of proposals, I believe any comments or questions would be helpful. Such contributes towards a conversation that will ultimately help us focus more review time on a smaller number of proposals. I’m first most interested in whether the proposal met all of the R-GSoC requirements and then Google’s GSoC requirements.

I’m also curious to see whether others detect in the proposal a commitment to staying involved after GSoC ends.
*
Thank you for taking the maintainer role for rtweet! Co-mentor Ben Ubah and I will monitor rtweet’s dev on GitHub and may  adjust R-GSoC work on our two rtweet-using projects. We appreciate the warning.

Rick Pack

On Fri, 19 Feb 2021, 5:27 am Brian G. Peterson, <br...@braverock.com> wrote:

> Potential GSoC Mentors,
>
> R has applied as mentoring organization again this year for Google Summer of Code 2021 (https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/how-it-works/) <https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/how-it-works/>.  While we won't know for a while if we have been accepted, we hope that we will be accepted again this year as we have been in past years.
>
> If you are an author or an R package, or have research using R that might benefit from additional paid summer coding help, I encourage you to consider positng a project idea to the R  GSoC wiki:
>
> https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/table%20of%20proposed%20coding%20projects
>
> start by copying the template here:
>
> https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/MENTORS-COPY-THIS-TEMPLATE
>
> into a separate project idea page, and add your project idea to the table on the first link above.
>
> In the coming couple of weeks, Google will evaluate organizations for inclusion in GSoC.  As part of that evaluation, Google reviews organization's project ideas.  So it is good for the R community to have project ideas in place for Google and potential students to review.
>
> Your project idea should encompass approximately 175 hours of paid work by a student over 10 weeks.  You should have at least two mentors for your project.  Please reach out to us with questions!
>
> Regards,
>
> Brian
>
> --

On Fri, Apr 16, 2021 at 6:19 PM Neeraj Dhanraj <neeraj...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Dear Brian Peterson,
>
> Could you please invite Prof. Andres Feijoo (afeijoo@uvigo) as a mentor for GSOC-R?
>
> Best,
> Neeraj
>
> On Fri, 19 Feb 2021, 5:27 am Brian G. Peterson, <br...@braverock.com> wrote:
> > Potential GSoC Mentors,
> >
> > R has applied as mentoring organization again this year for Google Summer of Code 2021 (https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/how-it-works/) <https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/how-it-works/>.  While we won't know for a while if we have been accepted, we hope that we will be accepted again this year as we have been in past years.
> >
> > If you are an author or an R package, or have research using R that might benefit from additional paid summer coding help, I encourage you to consider positng a project idea to the R  GSoC wiki:
> >
> > https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/table%20of%20proposed%20coding%20projects
> >
> > start by copying the template here:
> >
> > https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/MENTORS-COPY-THIS-TEMPLATE
> >
> > into a separate project idea page, and add your project idea to the table on the first link above.
> >
> > In the coming couple of weeks, Google will evaluate organizations for inclusion in GSoC.  As part of that evaluation, Google reviews organization's project ideas.  So it is good for the R community to have project ideas in place for Google and potential students to review.
> >
> > Your project idea should encompass approximately 175 hours of paid work by a student over 10 weeks.  You should have at least two mentors for your project.  Please reach out to us with questions!
> >
> > Regards,
> >
> > Brian
> >
> > --
> > Brian G. Peterson
> > ph: +1.773.459.4973
> > im: bgpbraverock
> >
